title: File:Cute Senior Small Poodle Mix.jpg
description: This dog has a very thin fur coat, and you can see his skin through his fur. He has lots of small splotches on his skin and his tail has very feathery and wispy strands of long hair hanging off of it. He is missing all of his incisors (front teeth), so his canine teeth are his front-most teeth. He has several small moles. He is very food motivated and loves most cats, humans, and other dogs. He has brown nails, eyes, eye liner, lips, gums, and a brown nose. He has a very deep voice for his size, but he is capable of making very high pitched sounds as well. He has been diagnosed with having a heart murmur, but he is very healthy and is in very good shape. He is very attached to his humans and he always wants to be around people.
author: Twawri

title: File:Tracker dogs, 1967.jpg
description: Two black Labrador dogs which had a lot of sniffing to do during Operation Lismore that was completed by 7th Battalion, The Royal Australian Regiment (7RAR). The dog handlers are 19983 Private (later Lance Corporal (L Cpl)) Thomas Douglas (Tom) Blackhurst of Swansea, NSW (left), with Justin and 43921 L Cpl Norman Leslie (Norm) Cameron of Kingston, SA, (right) with Cassius. The dogs were responsible for locating Viet Cong fighters and some enemy installations. L Cpl Blackhurst was killed in action on 17 April 1971 while serving with the Australian Army Training Team Vietnam. He was a radio operator, calling in helicopter of 9 Squadron RAAF for a medical evacuation. The helicopter crashed, killing L Cpl Blackhurst and 3170244 L Cpl John Francis Gillespie of 8 Field Ambulance, the medic on board.
author: Bryan Campbell (now at Australian War Memorial)
